paper_metadata.title: Anomalous increase of fracture toughness of TiAl-based alloys at high temperature

evidence.quote: The anomalous increase of mechanical property of TiAl-based alloys at high temperature caters to the property requirements as the high-temperature structural materials

The fracture toughness of TiAl-based alloys at high temperature indeed had an anomalous increase compared with that of room temperature. For the forged Ti-44Al-8Nb alloy, the average fracture toughness was 15.5 MPa·m1/2 at room temperature, 22.4 MPa·m1/2 at 700 °C, 21.9 MPa·m1/2 at 750 °C and 19.7 MPa·m1/2 at 800 °C, respectively.

other.raw_materials: Ti, Al and Al-Nb intermediate alloy with the purity of 99.99 wt%

evidence.quote: The cylindrical master alloy ingot with the nominal composition of Ti-44Al-8Nb and the size of about Ø 55 mm (diameter) × H150 mm (height) was prepared by electromagnetic cold crucible levitation melting technology.
Before forging, the billet with package was heated in a salt bath furnace at 1230 ± 10 ◦ C for 40 min.
Then, the billet was forged at the strain rate of about 0.01 s 1 , and the engineering strain was 50 %. The forged pancake removing the package was shown in Fig. 1 (c).
For the forged Ti-44Al-8Nb alloy, the average fracture toughness was 15.5 MPa·m1/2 at room temperature

mechanisms.name: anomalous increase of fracture toughness at high temperature

evidence.quote: There was such a causal relationship that led to the anomalous increase of fracture toughness at high temperature. It was “higher dislocation density in the microstructure” → “NSR2·δb2 > NSR1·δb1” (NSR1 ≈ 1) → “δy2bn|x=0 > δy1bn|x=0” → “F2 > F1” → KIC-high temperature > KIC-room temperature

mechanisms.name: dislocation slip on main slip surfaces

evidence.quote: The forging-induced texture, such as B2 < 100 > //RD and γ-TiAl < 011]//RD promoted the dislocations slip on the main slip surfaces during the high temperature fracture toughness test, contributing to the final high dislocation density.
